text:
Sara G: Heads up — I’m seeing a perf regression on Mixtral MoE after yesterday’s kernel selection tweak. p95 generation latency up ~40ms on 8k context workloads.
Nathan H: Can you paste the numbers and which job/cluster?
Sara G: Canary cluster mixtral-moex-prod-2, baseline p50=68ms p95=110ms. After change p50=74ms p95=150ms; tokens/s down ~20%. Non-MoE Llama runs look fine.
Liam P: Could be the RoPE rescale landing? We changed RoPE scaling + head dim normalization last week.
Sara G: Yeah regression correlates with that commit. Only shows up when sequence>4k and when top-k routing >16.
perf-bot: Profiling snapshot (short):
```
op                         | time_ms | note
kv_matmul                 | 38.6    | fallback to generic_gemm (no optimized kernel)
router_topk               | 24.1    | heavy scatter/gather
expert_dispatch           | 45.2    | memcpy spikes, cache misses
total_forward             | 148.9   | p95 spike
```
```
Kernel selector log: chose kernel "generic_gemm_f16" for head_dim=192 -> slow path.
```
Anita K: That explains a lot. Kernel selector has a cardinality table keyed by (head_dim, stride, alignment). RoPE rescale changed effective head_dim packing for Mixtral variants so we missed the fast path.
Nathan H: Also noticed elevated KV cache churn in the same runs. Expert cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 68% which amplifies router traffic. Mixing different seq lengths in batching seems to evict per-expert shards earlier.
Liam P: Two orthogonal knobs then: (1) get kernel selector to map the new head_dim to optimized kernel (or add a fallback hint), (2) reduce KV churn via batching and sticky sharding.
Sara G: Quick mitigations I tested locally:
- clamp router logits temperature (0.8 -> 0.6) to tighten expert distribution
- reduce top_k from 32 -> 16 for long context runs
- enable "kv_shard_sticky=true" so shards stick to the same device across micro-batches
- force kernel hint: `RUNTIME_KERNEL_HINT=fast_gemm_head192` for canary
Result: p95 back within ~5% of baseline and tokens/s ~95% recovered in A/B (small sample).
Nathan H: Can you share the CLI/config change you ran?
Sara G: gist of the canary config diff:
```
runtime:
  kernel_selector:
    hints:
      - head_dim: 192
        prefer: fast_gemm_f16
  routing:
    top_k: 16
    logits_temp: 0.6
  kv_cache:
    shard_sticky: true
```
Liam P: Good. Longer term we should: add automatic head_dim normalization in kernel selector, add a hotpath test in CI (mixtral-moex with long seq + varied seq batch), and instrument per-expert cache TTL.
Anita K: I opened INF-4892 (perf regression) and attached the profiling snapshot + A/B results.
perf-bot: INF-4892 created and assigned to eng-runtime. SLA: investigate -> mitigations within 24h.
Nathan H: Risk notes: forcing kernel hint is safe for canary but we need to validate numerics (fp16 kernels have slight roundoff). Also sticky KV sharding increases memory pressure on a node; watch OOM.
Sara G: Plan: ship routing clamps + kv_shard_sticky to canary group for 6h, observability dashboard for expert hit rates + kernel-path metric. Then next week push kernel-selector patch with head_dim aliasing. I’ll open the PR now.
Liam P: Also add synthetic replay harness that spikes mixed-length batches to catch this earlier.
Anita K: :thumbsup: tagging infra to bump canary retention to 12h and add perf alert on expert_cache_hit_rate<80%.
Sara G: Thanks — I’ll post updates in this thread once canary runs are green.
